text: The scope of sociological research covers almost all aspects of human society, and the core areas include: Theoretical Sociology: Exploring the fundamental principles of social operation, such as Marx's class theory, Weber's social stratification theory, and Durkheim's theory of social solidarity, to provide a bottom-level logical framework for understanding society.Applied Sociology: Focusing on specific social issues, such as poverty, inequality, educational equity, aging, urbanization, gender discrimination, and the internet society, for example, studying "the mental health of left-behind children and the social support system" and "the impact of short-video platforms on the values of teenagers".Social Structure and Stratification: Analyzing social classes, occupational differentiation, power distribution, etc., and exploring "why different groups have different resources and opportunities", such as the causes and effects of urban-rural gap and wealth disparity.Social Change and Development: Focusing on how society progresses from tradition to modernity, as well as the impacts of globalization, industrialization, and digitalization on society, for example, studying "the conflict between traditional customs and modernity in rural revitalization" and "the reshaping of employment structure by artificial intelligence".Culture and Social Interaction: Examining how cultural norms, values, and symbols shape social behavior, such as "the social function of the bride-price custom" and "the group identity behind online buzzwords".Social Organizations and Institutions: Studying the operational mechanisms of social organizations such as families, schools, enterprises, and governments, as well as the formation and role of social institutions such as laws, ethics, and religion, for example, "the impact of the change in modern family structure on the elderly care model".
